The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice for the published Sobolev interfaces cited below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and use real scalars. $L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$ means the $d$-tuple of real $L^2$ equivalence classes, with norm $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_{j=1}^d\|v_j\|_2^2$. The test space $C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ consists of real smooth functions compactly supported in $D$.

For $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$, say that $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ is its distributional divergence when
$$
\int_D v\cdot\nabla\phi\,dx=-\int_D g\phi\,dx\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R).
$$
The $L^2$ class $g$ is unique when it exists. Indeed, if $g_1,g_2$ both satisfy the identity, put $h=g_1-g_2\in L^2(D)$. Every compact $C\subset D$ has finite Lebesgue measure by [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] gives $\int_C|h|\le |C|^{1/2}\|h\|_{L^2(D)}<\infty$. Thus $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Subtracting the two divergence identities gives $\int_Dh\phi=0$ for every real test $\phi$; splitting a complex test into real and imaginary parts gives the same identity for complex tests. Injectivity of the regular-distribution map in [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] therefore yields $h=0$ almost everywhere, hence $g_1=g_2$ as $L^2$ classes. Define
$$
H(\operatorname{div};D):=\{v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d):\text{there is }g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)\text{ with }g=\operatorname{div}v\text{ distributionally}\},
$$
and equip it with the graph norm
$$
\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}:=\bigl(\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
$$
The Sobolev notation $H^1(D)=W^{1,2}(D)$ and $H^1_0(D)=W^{1,2}_0(D)$ uses the norm and zero-boundary closure conventions of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]. No pointwise boundary value is part of this definition.

Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev-space interfaces below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and $v\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$. Define the trace quotient
$$T_D:=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D),\qquad \|[w]\|_{T_D}:=\inf_{z\in H^1_0(D)}\|w+z\|_{H^1(D)}.$$
Then the formula
$$
\langle\gamma_n v,[w]\rangle:=\int_D\bigl(v\cdot\nabla w+(\operatorname{div}v)w\bigr)\,dx
$$
is independent of the representative $w$, defines a bounded real linear functional $\gamma_n v\in T_D'$, and satisfies $\|\gamma_n v\|_{T_D'}\le\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}$. This functional is the weak normal trace; no pointwise boundary value is asserted.

abla\delta u$ to get $g^2=(R_1z,
abla\delta u)+(R_2z,\delta u)$.

$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$

locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the

axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

$$

$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$

$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$

$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every

derivations.claim: H1 is complete: completeness of real $L^{2}$ [F6] gives limits in $L^{2}$ of a Cauchy sequence and each weak derivative satisfy distributional derivative identities by testing against compactly supported smooth functions and passing both integrals to their limits. H1_0 is closed by its closure definition. The scalar trace-quotient map is continuous because $\|[u|_K]\|_{H^1(K)/H^1_0(K)}\le\|u|_K\|_{H^1(K)}$ on each cell; the finite product preserves continuity. The normal map is continuous by [F2], again with a finite product. Thus both kernels are closed.

Let $\tau\in H(\operatorname{div};\Omega)$ and let an interior facet $F=K_+\cap K_-$ be fixed. For $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\operatorname{relint}F)$, choose a smooth function $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ supported in a small tubular neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$ meeting only $K_+$ and $K_-$ and having trace $\psi$ on $F$. The global distributional-divergence identity [F8] gives $\int_\Omega(\tau\cdot\nabla\phi+(\operatorname{div}\tau)\phi)=0$. Applying the cell Green identity [F2] to the two restrictions, with all other cell traces zero, yields $$\langle\gamma_{n_+,K_+}(\tau|_{K_+}),[\phi|_{K_+}]\rangle+\langle\gamma_{n_-,K_-}(\tau|_{K_-}),[\phi|_{K_-}]\rangle=0.$$ The two cell trace classes in this equation restrict to the same $\psi$ on $F$ and vanish on the other facets. Since this holds for every such $\psi$, the two outward weak normal traces cancel as distributions on the relative interior of each interior facet. This is the conservative facet relation for a global H(div) lift; it uses the distributional divergence identity and weak Green formula, not pointwise normal values.

For a closed subspace $M$ of a Hilbert space, a distance-minimizing sequence is Cauchy by the parallelogram identity; its limit is nearest, and variation along $M$ makes the residual orthogonal. Thus $H=M\oplus M^\perp$ and $H/M$ is isometric to $M^\perp$. Applying this to both kernels in step 1.1 proves the quotient ranges are Hilbert with their infimum norms.

Global lifts restrict to broken lifts; conversely the admissible broken extensions in the Statement are exactly those gluing to a global lift, so the two infima have the same set. Cell scalar traces are bounded by [F3] and those of a global H1 lift match across interior facets by [F4]; normal traces of a global H(div) lift satisfy the cancellation proved in step 1.2. Thus range membership is precisely the stated compatibility, with the global lift infimum norms.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d=2$ or $3$, $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral and $\mathcal T_h$ a finite conforming shape-regular simplicial partition; all fields are real. For a load $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, put $H(div,\mathcal T_h)=\prod_KH(div;K)$ and $H^1(\mathcal T_h)=\prod_KH^1(K)$, with squared broken graph norm $\sum_K(\|	au\|_2^2+\|div	au\|_2^2+\|v\|_2^2+\|
abla v\|_2^2)$. Let $\widehat U$ be the elementwise trace range of $H^1_0(\Omega)$ and $\widehat Q_n$ the elementwise weak normal trace range of $H(div;\Omega)$, each with global lift infimum norm; range membership is compatibility and normal traces are conservative across interior facets. Set $U=L^2(\Omega)^d	imes L^2(\Omega)	imes\widehat U	imes\widehat Q_n$, $V=H(div,\mathcal T_h)	imes H^1(\mathcal T_h)$. For $x=(\sigma,u,\widehat u,\widehat\sigma_n)$ and $y=(	au,v)$, define
$$b(x,y)=(\sigma,	au)-(u,div_h	au)+\langle\widehat u,	au\cdot nangle-(\sigma,
abla_hv)+\langle\widehat\sigma_n,vangle,\quad F_f(y)=(f,v).$$
Pairings sum over cell boundaries and use the cell-outward normal. The sign convention is $\sigma=-
abla u$, $div\sigma=f$.

Assume Countable Choice and [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. The elementwise trace map $\Gamma_0:H^1_0(\Omega)\to\prod_KH^1(K)/H^1_0(K)$ and normal-trace map $\Gamma_n:H(div;\Omega)\to\prod_K(H^1(K)/H^1_0(K))'$ have real Hilbert quotient ranges with global lift infimum norms. These equal the infima over broken extensions whose gluing belongs to the respective global space. Compatibility means membership in these ranges, so normal traces are conservative on each interior facet in the weak distributional sense.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded, connected polyhedral Lipschitz domain. A matching affine simplicial mesh and its shape regularity have the exact meaning of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]; additionally, call the mesh facet-connected when its dual graph (one vertex per cell and one edge per shared $(d-1)$-facet) is connected. Write $h=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\operatorname{diam}K$.

For $k\ge0$, $\mathbb P_k(K)$ is the real scalar polynomial space of total degree at most $k$, and $\widetilde{\mathbb P}_k$ is the real homogeneous scalar polynomial space of degree exactly $k$ (for $k=0$, the constants). Define
$$\operatorname{RT}_k(K)=\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb R^d)+x\widetilde{\mathbb P}_k(K),\qquad \operatorname{BDM}_k(K)=\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb R^d)\quad(k\ge1).$$
For either local family $X_k$, its global H(div)-conforming space is
$$X_k(\mathcal T_h)=\{v\in H(\operatorname{div};D):v|_K\in X_k(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T_h\}.
$$
The zero-normal RT0 flux space and mean-zero P0 pressure space are
$$V_h:=\operatorname{RT}_0(\mathcal T_h)\cap H_0(\operatorname{div};D),\qquad Q_h:=\{q\in L^2(D):q|_K\text{ is constant for every }K,\ \int_Dq=0\}.$$
For each mesh facet $F$, fix one unit normal $n_F$; on a cell boundary use the outward unit normal $n_K$, which equals either $n_F$ or $-n_F$. The notation $\mathbb P_0(\mathcal T_h)$ means cellwise constants. No existence of a mesh for every $D$ is asserted by this definition.

Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev-space interfaces below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and $v\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$. Define the trace quotient
$$T_D:=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D),\qquad \|[w]\|_{T_D}:=\inf_{z\in H^1_0(D)}\|w+z\|_{H^1(D)}.$$
Then the formula
$$
\langle\gamma_n v,[w]\rangle:=\int_D\bigl(v\cdot\nabla w+(\operatorname{div}v)w\bigr)\,dx
$$
is independent of the representative $w$, defines a bounded real linear functional $\gamma_n v\in T_D'$, and satisfies $\|\gamma_n v\|_{T_D'}\le\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}$. This functional is the weak normal trace; no pointwise boundary value is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. For a nondegenerate affine simplex $K$ with diameter $h_K$ and shape bound $h_K/r_K\le\gamma$, and any facet $F$, every $u\in H^1(K)$ has a well-defined trace $\gamma_Fu\in L^2(F)$ and
$$
\|\gamma_Fu\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C(d,\gamma)\bigl(h_K^{-1}\|u\|_{L^2(K)}^2+h_K\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(K)}^2\bigr).
$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Assume Countable Choice. For every $1\le p<\infty$ there is
$C_{d,p}<\infty$ such that for all
$u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)$,
$$\|u-u_{\widehat S_d}\|_{L^p(\widehat S_d)} \le C_{d,p}|u|_{W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)},\qquad u_{\widehat S_d}:=|\widehat S_d|^{-1}\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,dx.$$

Let $\widehat K,K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nondegenerate open simplices and let $F_K:\widehat K\to K$ be the orientation-preserving affine bijection $F_K(\widehat x)=A_K\widehat x+b_K$, where $J_K:=\det A_K>0$. For a measurable vector field $\widehat v$ on $\widehat K$, define its contravariant Piola push-forward by
$$
(\mathcal P_K\widehat v)(x):=J_K^{-1}A_K\widehat v(F_K^{-1}(x)),\qquad x\in K.
$$
The inverse pull-back is $\widehat v(\widehat x)=J_KA_K^{-1}v(F_K(\widehat x))$. Facet normals are oriented consistently with the chosen orientation of $F_K$; the associated oriented surface vector transforms by $n\,ds=J_KA_K^{-T}\widehat n\,d\widehat s$.

Let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ be an orientation-preserving affine bijection between nondegenerate $d$-simplices, with $J=\det A>0$, and use the contravariant Piola map of [[def-na-contravariant-piola-map]]. For every $k\ge0$, it maps $\operatorname{RT}_k(\widehat K)$ bijectively onto $\operatorname{RT}_k(K)$, and for every $k\ge1$ it maps $\operatorname{BDM}_k(\widehat K)$ bijectively onto $\operatorname{BDM}_k(K)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d=2$ or $3$ and let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ map a reference
simplex to an affine cell with $\det A>0$. The contravariant Piola map
$\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{div}}\widehat v=(\det A)^{-1}A\widehat v\circ F^{-1}$
maps $H(\operatorname{div},\widehat S_d)$ into $H(\operatorname{div},K)$ and
$$\operatorname{div}(\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{div}}\widehat v) =(\det A)^{-1}(\widehat{\operatorname{div}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}.$$
The covariant Piola map
$\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{curl}}\widehat v=A^{-T}\widehat v\circ F^{-1}$
maps $H(\operatorname{curl},\widehat S_d)$ into $H(\operatorname{curl},K)$;
in $d=2$ its scalar curl is
$(\det A)^{-1}(\widehat{\operatorname{curl}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}$,
and in $d=3$ its vector curl is
$(\det A)^{-1}A(\widehat{\operatorname{curl}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}$.
For every $\widehat u\in W^{1,2}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)$, the scalar
pullback $u=\widehat u\circ F^{-1}$ belongs to $W^{1,2}(K;\mathbb R)$ and
its gradient satisfies
$$\nabla u=\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{curl}}(\widehat\nabla\widehat u).$$
For smooth fields, contravariant normal fluxes satisfy
$v\cdot n\,dS=\widehat v\cdot\widehat n\,d\widehat S$; covariant tangential
pullbacks satisfy $v(F(\widehat x))\cdot A\widehat\tau=
\widehat v(\widehat x)\cdot\widehat\tau$ for every reference tangent
$\widehat\tau$. Thus edge line integrals and normal-flux moments are
preserved, and face tangential moments transform with this pullback and
the induced facet surface Jacobian. These formulas record the chosen
orientation; reversing a facet orientation reverses its signed moment.

Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev-space interfaces below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and $v\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$. Define the trace quotient
$$T_D:=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D),\qquad \|[w]\|_{T_D}:=\inf_{z\in H^1_0(D)}\|w+z\|_{H^1(D)}.$$
Then the formula
$$
\langle\gamma_n v,[w]\rangle:=\int_D\bigl(v\cdot\nabla w+(\operatorname{div}v)w\bigr)\,dx

In the homogeneous system an edge restriction is $t(1-t)(a+bt)$; testing against $a+bt$ forces its weighted square integral to vanish. Each edge restriction is zero, leaving $c\lambda_0\lambda_1\lambda_2$, whose mean forces $c=0$. Hence the seven scalar moments are unisolvent.

On the reference triangle $RT_2=P_2^2+x\widetilde P_2$ has dimension $15$. Its normal trace map is onto broken P2: for an edge $F$ opposite vertex $a_i$, extend any $q\in P_2(F)$ polynomially in the other two barycentric coordinates and set $	au=(x-a_i)q(x)/H_i$, where $H_i$ is the altitude to $F$. This vector is tangent to the other two edges and has normal trace $q$ on $F$; it lies in $RT_2$ because its cubic part is $x$ times a homogeneous degree-two polynomial and its remaining terms lie in $P_2^2$. Thus the broken normal trace image has dimension $9$. Let $B^{div}_3$ be its inverse image of continuous P2 boundary traces, a $12$-dimensional subspace. Define $\Pi^{div}_3	au\in B^{div}_3$ by matching six volume moments against $P_1^2$ and six continuous boundary P2 normal moments. In the homogeneous system the normal trace is continuous P2 and orthogonal to itself, hence zero. Green’s identity and $
abla P_2\subset P_1^2$ then give $div	au=0$; its homogeneous cubic part $xq_2$ has divergence $4q_2$, so $	au\in P_2^2$. Write $	au=R
abla\phi$: explicitly, for polynomial $	au=(	au_1,	au_2)$ use $\phi(x,y)=\int_0^x	au_2(s,0)\,ds-\int_0^y	au_1(x,t)\,dt$. The identity $\partial_x	au_1+\partial_y	au_2=0$ gives $\partial_x\phi=	au_2$ and $\partial_y\phi=-	au_1$, and $\deg\phi\le3$. Zero normal trace makes $\phi$ constant on each edge; vertex continuity makes these constants equal. After subtracting the common constant, $\phi=c\lambda_0\lambda_1\lambda_2$. The volume moment against $Rx$ is $\int_K
abla\phi\cdot x=-2c\int_K\lambda_0\lambda_1\lambda_2$ by Green’s identity and $\phi|_{\partial K}=0$, so $c=0$. Thus the 12 moments are unisolvent.

On the reference triangle set $\widehat\Pi^{grad}_3\widehat v=\bar{\widehat v}+\Pi^0_3(\widehat v-\bar{\widehat v})$; for a physical cell let $F_K(\widehat x)=A_K\widehat x+b_K$ be its orientation-preserving affine map and define $\Pi^{grad}_{3,K}v=(\widehat\Pi^{grad}_3(v\circ F_K))\circ F_K^{-1}$. The bounded inverse reference moment matrix, [F5], mean-zero Poincare–Wirtinger [F7], and shape scaling [F6] yield $\|\Pi^{grad}_{3,K}v\|_{H^1(K)}\le C\|v\|_{H^1(K)}$ and $\|v-\Pi^{grad}_{3,K}v\|_2\le Ch_K\|\nabla v\|_2$.

Applying [F8] to the affine inverse shows $\widehat\tau\in H(\operatorname{div};\widehat K)$ with the transformed divergence. Define the physical projection by $\Pi^{div}_{3,K}\tau:=\mathcal P_K(\widehat\Pi^{div}_3\widehat\tau)$. For every $w\in H^1(K)$, $w\circ F_K\in H^1(\widehat K)$ by [F8], and the weak Green functional, affine weak-derivative/divergence transformations, and change of variables give $$\langle\gamma_{n,K}\tau,[w]\rangle=\int_{\widehat K}\bigl(\widehat\tau\cdot\widehat\nabla(w\circ F_K)+(\widehat{\operatorname{div}}\widehat\tau)(w\circ F_K)\bigr) =\langle\gamma_{\widehat n,\widehat K}\widehat\tau,[w\circ F_K]\rangle.$$ The volume moments also transport: for $p\in P_1(K)^2$, affine change of variables gives $$(\Pi^{div}_3\tau,p)_K=(\widehat\Pi^{div}_3\widehat\tau,A_K^{\mathsf T}(p\circ F_K))_{\widehat K},\qquad A_K^{\mathsf T}(p\circ F_K)\in P_1(\widehat K)^2,$$ and the same identity with $\widehat\Pi^{div}_3\widehat\tau$ replaced by $\widehat\tau$; hence every physical $P_1(K)^2$ volume moment is matched. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching
affine simplicial mesh, let $1\le p<\infty$, and let $v$ be a real-valued
conforming piecewise polynomial whose polynomial trace vanishes on every boundary
facet. Then
$$v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega),\qquad \|v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Here $W^{1,p}_0$ is the norm closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; no C1
trace characterization is used.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice for the published Sobolev interfaces cited below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and use real scalars. $L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$ means the $d$-tuple of real $L^2$ equivalence classes, with norm $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_{j=1}^d\|v_j\|_2^2$. The test space $C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ consists of real smooth functions compactly supported in $D$.

For $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$, say that $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ is its distributional divergence when
$$
\int_D v\cdot\nabla\phi\,dx=-\int_D g\phi\,dx\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R).
$$
The $L^2$ class $g$ is unique when it exists. Indeed, if $g_1,g_2$ both satisfy the identity, put $h=g_1-g_2\in L^2(D)$. Every compact $C\subset D$ has finite Lebesgue measure by [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] gives $\int_C|h|\le |C|^{1/2}\|h\|_{L^2(D)}<\infty$. Thus $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Subtracting the two divergence identities gives $\int_Dh\phi=0$ for every real test $\phi$; splitting a complex test into real and imaginary parts gives the same identity for complex tests. Injectivity of the regular-distribution map in [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] therefore yields $h=0$ almost everywhere, hence $g_1=g_2$ as $L^2$ classes. Define
$$
H(\operatorname{div};D):=\{v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d):\text{there is }g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)\text{ with }g=\operatorname{div}v\text{ distributionally}\},
$$
and equip it with the graph norm
$$
\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}:=\bigl(\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
$$
The Sobolev notation $H^1(D)=W^{1,2}(D)$ and $H^1_0(D)=W^{1,2}_0(D)$ uses the norm and zero-boundary closure conventions of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]. No pointwise boundary value is part of this definition.
